subject: ACME Retail marketplace private order: rev-share and billing exception request
messages:
From: Emily Tan <emily.tan@acmeretail.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmeretail.com
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Private marketplace order + rev-share note

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo last week. ACME is ready to move forward with a private listing on the AWS Marketplace, but procurement has three asks before signature:

1) A 10% off standard list pricing for year 1 (applied across quote SKU line items)
2) Net-60 billing terms (ACME standard) with invoice via Redwood; AWS marketplace must reflect settlement cadence
3) Rev-share alignment: ACME requires a 20% partner revenue split to appear on the marketplace listing so they can co-market as part of their deployment program

We understand some of these are non-standard. Attached is our procurement checklist (acme_requirements.pdf) and a sample purchase order. If possible, could you confirm what exceptions Redwood can approve vs what needs exec signoff? We need to return a redline by EOW.

Appreciate it — Emily
Emily Tan
Director, Strategic Procurement
ACME Retail

---
Attachment: acme_requirements.pdf (application/pdf, 210 KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Emily Tan <emily.tan@acmeretail.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Private marketplace order + rev-share note

Hi Emily — thanks for the clarity and the checklist. Looping in Aditya (AE), Markus (Finance) and Logan (Legal/Marketplace) so we can confirm feasibility.

Quick internal summary of the asks:
- 10% off list for year 1
- Net-60 billing
- Marketplace rev-share set at 20% to ACME (ACME expects the partner split visible on AWS)

What I can act on: small promotional discounts for year 1 (under 12%) are within my delegated authority for standard PO value thresholds. Anything >= 12% or changes to billing cadence or marketplace rev-share percentages likely require deal-desk escalation and executive approval.

Proposed initial data point for internal review:
- Discount: 8–10% for year 1 (depending on term / minimum commitment)
- Billing: propose Net-45 instead of Net-60 to reduce AR risk; if finance approves Net-60, we need exec signoff
- Rev-share: recommend we treat AWS rev-share as a separate carve (we can set listing split, but Redwood's payout to AWS/partner is constrained by marketplace fees). Operationally, offering ACME 20% on the customer-facing split would push Redwood's economics below our typical floor unless offset by a 2–3 year commitment or minimum usage guarantee.

Attached: draft SOW and a quick financial model I built. Please review and advise on risk tolerance. If we need to escalate to execs, I will prepare a short one-pager for signoff.

Thanks,
Olga
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: redwood_draft_sow_v3.docx, financial_impact_model.xlsx

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: Private marketplace order + rev-share note

Folks — reviewed the model. High-level finance position:

- 20% listed rev-share to ACME is not sustainable without a corroborating commit. Our unit margin at that rev-share is negative for first 12 months under the proposed pricing.
- Net-60 increases DSO materially; if we accept Net-60, we need either (a) an increased price or (b) a 60-day financing fee passed to the buyer.
- If we cap ACME's listed rev-share to 15%, Redwood retains better economics and we can offer the remaining credit back to ACME as marketing funds (one-off) to preserve their go-to-market objectives.

I ran two scenarios in the sheet: (A) 10% discount + 15% listed rev-share + Net-45 = acceptable; (B) 10% discount + 20% listed rev-share + Net-60 = requires executive approval and ~1.8M incremental headroom in the first year to avoid a loss.

Recommend we attempt to close on scenario A and reserve scenario B as an exec-only exception tied to a 3-year committed minimum.

-Markus
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: Private marketplace order + rev-share note

+1 to Olga's plan — from AE perspective this is a strategic logo and reference account for retail. A few points: 

- ACME will push hard on 20% unless we give them something else. They're looking for co-marketing and visibility on AWS as part of a larger integration play.
- We should try to bridge with a conditional structure: 18% listed rev-share in year 1 if ACME agrees to a 2-year commit with minimum monthly consumption tiers and joint-marketing credits capped at X. If they under-consume, rev-share steps down to 12% in year 2.
- For billing: Net-45 + bulk prepayment credit (if they want Net-60, they can accept a small financing fee or a slightly lower discount).

If we can get leadership to pre-approve a boxed exception (exec signoff conditioned on the 2-year commit + minimums), we can close this quickly and preserve economics. Happy to draft the conditional clause for SOW.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Requesting executive exception: ACME Retail AWS Marketplace private listing (decision required)

Laura — 

We need an executive decision on a private marketplace exception for ACME Retail (Deal: ACME-PO-2028-0425). Summary: ACME requests 10% off list (year 1), Net-60 billing, and a 20% customer-facing revenue split on the AWS Marketplace listing.

Background / impacts:
- Finance (Markus) flags that 20% listed rev-share with the 10% discount + Net-60 produces negative margin in year 1 without a minimum commitment. He recommends capping listed rev-share at 15% and Net-45 billing, or requiring a 3-year committed minimum to make 20% sustainable.
- Sales (Aditya) requests an exec-boxed exception: approve up to 18% listed rev-share for year 1 conditioned on a 2-year commitment and hard monthly consumption minimums; accept Net-45 by default; allow Net-60 only if ACME accepts a small financing fee or prepayment credit.
- Legal/Marketplace (Logan) notes AWS private listing mechanics: we can set the customer-visible split on the listing, but Redwood remains responsible for settlement to AWS and must ensure our seller terms cover any downstream payout; AWS may also have limits on listing splits that require doc review.

Requested decision: Please approve one of the following options so we can return to ACME today:
A) Approve exec exception: up to 18% listed rev-share for year 1 conditioned on 2-year committed minimum + minimum monthly usage (Redwood to absorb economics per attached model). Net-45 default, Net-60 only with financing fee.
B) Approve fallback: 10% discount + 15% listed rev-share + Net-45 (no exec exception required).
C) Decline marketplace listing; pursue direct private contract instead (longer closing timeline).

Attachments included: redwood_draft_sow_v3.docx, financial_impact_model.xlsx.

If you prefer, I can present this in the 9am leadership huddle tomorrow for a quick vote — we need a response to ACME by EOW.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
